body:
Found while assessing RTL/Arabic for [[T-111]], but it is a present-day bug with
nothing to do with i18n.

## Problem

All three codebases validate a price amount with what LOOKS like the same
regex — `^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$`:

- `server/src/shoppinglist_server/sync.py`  PRICE_AMOUNT_RE
- `web/src/lib/priceParse.ts`               PRICE_AMOUNT_RE
- `android .../ui/item/ItemFormViewModel.kt` PRICE_AMOUNT_RE

`\d` does not mean the same thing in all three. Verified by running each:

| runtime | `^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$` vs `٥.٩٩` |
|---|---|
| JS (web client)      | rejects |
| JVM (Android client) | rejects |
| **Python (server)**  | **accepts** |

Python's `\d` is Unicode-aware for `str` patterns, so it matches Eastern Arabic,
Devanagari and every other Unicode decimal digit. JS `\d` and Java/Kotlin `\d`
are ASCII-only by default.

So the server is strictly MORE permissive than every one of its own clients, and
the discrepancy is invisible on inspection because the regex source text is
character-for-character identical in all three files.

## Impact

`price_amount` is stored and synced as a TEXT decimal string. Anything that
bypasses the two clients — curl, a future client, a client whose own validation
is weaker — can push `٥.٩٩`, the server accepts and stores it, and it is then
served to every member of the list. Both real clients fail to parse it:
`parseFloat("٥.٩٩")` is `NaN`. So one crafted row can render as NaN (or worse,
depending on the consumer) for everyone in the list, and it survives in the
database.

Same family as the T-85 field-validation hardening, which bounded types and
lengths on every /sync field; this one slipped through because the regex looked
right.

## Fix

Anchor the server regex to ASCII digits so the door matches the clients:

    PRICE_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$")

Prefer the explicit character class over `re.ASCII` — it is local, obvious, and
cannot be undone by someone later recompiling the pattern without the flag.

Then sweep the rest of the server for the same trap: any `\d` in a pattern
validating a wire value that clients produce with ASCII-only semantics. Check at
least `CURRENCY_RE`, the invite token fields, and anything added since T-85.

## Verification

- Server test asserting `٥.٩٩`, `١٩٩` and Devanagari digits are all rejected with
  the existing `invalid_price` 422.
- A test asserting the three regexes agree, or at minimum a comment in each of
  the three files pointing at the other two and at this ticket — the failure mode
  here is precisely that they look identical and are not.
title: server accepts non-ASCII digits in a price; both clients reject them
